title: A cycle supported in an open ball annihilates every test form that is constant on that ball
statement: Assume (VO), the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, which appears verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let X ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ (n+1)) be a current, x₀ ∈ ℝ^P, r a real number with r > 0, α an (n+1)-covector (Covector (Euclid P) (n+1)) and φ ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ (n+1)) a test form. Suppose ∂X = 0 (X.boundary = 0), spt X ⊆ B_r(x₀) (the open ball), and φ(x) = α for every x ∈ B_r(x₀). Then X(φ) = 0.
lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)) (x₀ : Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)), 0 < r → X.boundary = 0 → X.support ⊆ ball x₀ r → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ r, (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1)) x = α) → X φ = 0
